gloss: ritual clapping at a Shinto shrine

definitions.explanation: The ceremonial clapping performed when worshipping at a Shinto shrine, typically two claps with the palms slightly offset to produce a clear, resonant sound that calls the attention of the {神|かみ}.

examples.japanese: {神社|じんじゃ}で{柏手|かしわで}を{打|う}った。
examples.english: I clapped my hands ritually at the shrine.

examples.japanese: {二礼|にれい}{二|に}{拍手|はくしゅ}{一礼|いちれい}と{言|い}って、{柏手|かしわで}を{二回|にかい}{打|う}つ。
examples.english: It's called "two bows, two claps, one bow," and you clap your hands twice.

examples.japanese: {出雲大社|いずもたいしゃ}では、{他|ほか}の{神社|じんじゃ}と{違|ちが}って{柏手|かしわで}を{四回|よんかい}{打|う}つのが{習|なら}わしだ。
examples.english: At Izumo Taisha, unlike other shrines, the custom is to clap four times.

notes:
The kanji {柏|かしわ} (oak) is used here for historical phonetic reasons rather than meaning. Sometimes written in hiragana as かしわで.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {柏手|かしわで}を{打|う}つ: to clap ritually (the standard verb is {打|う}つ, not the everyday {叩|たた}く)
- {柏手|かしわで}の{音|おと}: the sound of ritual clapping
- {二|に}{拍手|はくしゅ}: two claps (modern term for the same act)

CULTURAL NOTE:
The standard pattern at most Shinto shrines is {二礼|にれい}{二|に}{拍手|はくしゅ}{一礼|いちれい}: bow twice, clap twice, bow once. The right hand is positioned slightly lower than the left to produce a clearer sound. {出雲大社|いずもたいしゃ} and {宇佐神宮|うさじんぐう} use four claps instead of two.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {拍手|はくしゅ}: applause; also used in the formal expression {二拍手|にはくしゅ} for ritual clapping
- {手|て}を{合|あ}わせる: to put one's hands together — the gesture used at Buddhist temples instead of clapping
